01 / THE SOURCE

The map is real.
The learning experiment is ours.

Google, HHMI Janelia and collaborators reconstructed the male fruit fly’s brain and ventral nerve cord, reporting over 166,000 neurons and about 125 million synaptic connections. It gives researchers anatomical routes to investigate and compare, including differences between sexes. Google Research ↗

FLY uses the released MaleCNS connectivity and skeletons. Our neural dynamics, sensory approximation, output labels and learning rule are additional hypotheses. The source publication did not train this model to answer citizenship questions.

Research componentWhat this experiment does
Anatomical graphRetains 166,700 neurons, 25,582,938 directed cell-to-cell edges and 124,177,617 aggregated contacts. Manifest
Neuron geometryDisplays 630 sampled original skeletons. The simulation retains the full graph. Display record
Cell identity and routesThe revised control uses visual KCg-d cells and MBON09/27/05/01 outputs, selected from their anatomical connectivity.
Dynamics and plasticityCustom LIF parameters, declared gain changes and supervised local updates. These are not parameters measured or validated by Google.
Fly animationNeuroMechFly anatomy with illustrative motion. Recorded model spikes do not drive a validated motor controller.

A contact count is not a measured physiological connection strength. Anatomical fidelity and dynamical fidelity need separate evidence. Read the full source audit ↗

02 / THE LEARNING RESULT

Same wiring.
Some connections learned.

We randomly selected four disjoint groups of 16 visual Kenyon cells and directly stimulated one group at a time. This deliberately isolates the learning mechanism from the unresolved retina-to-memory pathway. It presents neural signals, not German text.

Across 128 training presentations, a supervised local rule changed only existing KC-to-output connection weights. Training labels enter those weight updates. Frozen evaluation receives the neural stimulus alone; the choice comes from the designated output neurons’ firing rates.

Frozen evaluationFirst ensemblesNew ensembles
Untrained9/328/32
Trained32/3230/32
Shuffled training labels8/320/32
Connection weights changed178244

Each evaluation uses fresh drive amplitudes for four familiar ensembles. The replication selects different neurons and uses new seeds. It is replication within one computational model, not a second animal, unseen language or an independent biological validation. A matched topology control has not yet tested whether the specific measured wiring is necessary for this task.

Reloading the first checkpoint reproduced every evaluated total spike count, output rate and choice. Restoring its initial learned weights returned performance to 9/32. Silencing Kenyon cells yielded 0/32. Verification records ↗

The two training runs each contain 51.2 simulated seconds. Their accumulated neural-kernel times were 1.780 and 3.943 seconds, excluding setup, Python orchestration, logging and analysis. These sparse direct-stimulation workloads do not predict the runtime or convergence of citizenship training.

03 / THE UNSOLVED PART

Learning a signal
is only the first step.

The visual route remains the obstacle. We logged 110 calibration trials across 22 configurations. None met the predeclared combination of sparse activity, distinguishable responses and bounded output rates. The model tended toward silence or broad activation.

The audit also exposed an uneven retinal projection: the original four quadrants contained 1,070, 1,487, 78 and 700 mapped receptors. Two initially chosen answer populations had no direct input from KCg-d. Correcting coverage and choosing anatomically connected outputs improved the experiment’s design, but did not establish visual learning.

The positive control therefore cannot substitute for the visual gate. A claim that the fly model reads, understands civics, or passes the test would go beyond these results.

04 / THE GERMAN TEST

The original challenge
is still the goal.

The next experiment must calibrate the sensory pathway against biological visual-response evidence, then demonstrate the fixed four-way visual task with frozen evaluation and controls. Only then does citizenship training begin with a small, verified question bank.

Recognizing familiar catalogue questions and understanding new German questions are different targets. We will test option reordering and new renderings, record every failure, and keep the final grader separate from inference. There is no defensible time-to-pass estimate yet.

The original 33-question sitting remains an untrained baseline: 0/33, all abstentions. It is a software practice selection, not an official BAMF examination. Inspect the original attempt ↗
